alignment.note: the reproduction is this far from where the original has the same floor

P1.reason: The overall arrangement matches. Both have an octagonal hall split by a north-south central corridor (the plans, x 395-478 in the original, x 1355-1443 in the reproduction), an east annex with stairs, a western side room, the south ladder spur and the sunken central octagon at z 0. The joins inside the hall differ, though. In the original's z 228 storey, an outer ring corridor wraps the four quadrant rooms and is walled off from them by diagonal walls, and hexagonal pits flank the corridor (the dark grey areas in the plan). The reproduction has one big central octagon floor at the corridor instead of the two flanking pits. Its outer ring mostly opens into the quadrant rooms, without the original's inner diagonal partitions. It also adds a rectangular floor in the south-east quadrant (plan, around x 1450-1560, y 630-700) that the original lacks. Views 5, 6 and 7 confirm it: the original's starts face a close wall, while the same points in the reproduction look into open rooms.

P2.reason: The measured floor overlap is 0.716 with no offset, just above the 0.70 line. Overall extents are 2440 x 2088 x 672 against 2432 x 2080 x 672. The hall, the central corridor (north and south ends at the same places), the east annex and the west wing are at matching sizes and places, within about 10%. The partition differences inside the hall are counted under P1.

P3.reason: The sections agree closely. Both have floors at z 0, 160, 320 and 512 in the same spans, the same stepped ceiling block in the middle, the z 160 ledges left and right, the low z 0 rooms under them with the same dividing walls, and the right-hand room at z 160 near x 800. The storeys show the same z 0 / 160 / 320 / 512 values per area, and the east annex has its stairs in the same place. Small offsets remain. The original's top floors run to 542, 371 and 192, against 512, 320 and 176 in the reproduction, so a couple of ledges sit 16 to 50 units off. None of that changes the shape of the levels.

P4.reason: 54 of 58 entities are matched (93.1%, above 80%). Starts, weapons, ammo, the longjump, batteries, the health charger, the func_doors with their trigger_multiple, the ladders and the func_walls are all in the original's places. Two weapon_tripmine (at -816 272 176 and -816 -288 176) and two ammo_ARgrenades (at -936 808 184 and -128 -808 184) are missing or misplaced.

P5.reason: The original's walls are blue-grey concrete panels with recessed rounded windows full of computer banks, a yellow stripe along the bottom and a light tiled floor (views 1, 2, 3 and 8). The reproduction uses a warmer brown-grey concrete and a flat black-and-green blinking panel texture in place of the windowed computer banks, with a darker tile floor and no yellow trim. A player would see the difference straight away.

P6.reason: The light entities in the east annex sit in the same places, but the look differs. The original lights its corridors with recessed ceiling fixtures (view 8) and leaves the start points in views 5, 6 and 7 quite dark. The reproduction uses bright white wall-mounted strip lamps (views 2, 3, 4, 7) and lights the open areas brighter, with hot spots on the walls the original lacks. The overall brightness pattern differs from the original's.

P7.reason: The central corridor and the octagonal hall are there, with the square pillars in each quadrant (the plan's small squares) in place. The original's most distinctive detail is missing: the rounded window frames holding the computer banks, separated by concrete pilasters (views 1, 2, 3, 8). So are the yellow lower trim and the floor grates seen in view 3. The flat panels in the reproduction stand in for them only loosely.

P8.reason: There are no check errors, and the walk test finds 0 unreached items from the reproduction's starts (the original has 3 unreached). It compiles, does not leak and stays within the engine's limits.

P9.reason: From the same points, most views do not look like the same place. Start 1: the original faces two windowed computer banks on concrete, the reproduction a dark blank wall with a small panel. Start 3: the original shows a room lined with computer windows and a yellow stripe, the reproduction a plain wall and a lamp. Start 4: the original is a close concrete wall, the reproduction a long lit corridor. Starts 5, 6 and 7: the original is a dark close wall of consoles, the reproduction open rooms with bright lamps. Only start 8 (a corridor lined with consoles) and, loosely, start 2 resemble the original, and even those lose the windowed frames and the original's colours. A player who knows the map would not recognise it at once.
